# AGENTS.md — Operating rules for AI coding agents

Project: **StockSync** · Stack: Node.js 22 LTS, TypeScript (strict), ESLint (typescript-eslint), Vitest · Autonomy: **phase** · Checkpoints: `after-plan`, `after-phase`, `before-deploy`

You are a senior engineer working inside the **AI Project Engine**. The engine CLI (`node engine/engine.mjs`) owns the workflow:
it picks tasks, extracts context, runs quality gates, records progress and commits. **Use it — never imitate it by hand.**

## 1. Lifecycle (one command per phase)
| Phase | Command | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Discovery | `/engine-start` | `engine.config.jsonc` + `docs/1_PRD.md` filled, open questions answered |
| 1 Plan | `/engine-plan` | docs 2–4 + `.env.example`; **STOP** for human approval (`node engine/engine.mjs approve plan`) |
| 2 Build | `/engine-build` | tasks done via `next → TDD → gate → done`; stops per autonomy/checkpoints |
| 2b Review | `/engine-review` | read-only review of the phase; fixes filed as new tasks |
| 3 Audit | `/engine-audit` | `docs/7_SECURITY_AUDIT.md`, fixes, all gates green |
| 4 Deploy | `/engine-deploy` | containers, CI/CD, IaC, `docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` (needs `approve deploy`) |
| any | `/engine-resume`, `/engine-replan` | recover after /clear · change scope safely |

## 2. The build loop (never skip a step)
1. `node engine/engine.mjs next` → read **only** `docs/5_CURRENT_TASK.md` and the files it lists. It already contains the acceptance criteria and the extracted contract sections.
2. Write a failing test first; run it; confirm it fails for the expected reason.
3. Implement the minimum code to pass. Surgical edits — don't rewrite files you only touch slightly.
4. `node engine/engine.mjs gate`. Fix the **root cause** of failures. Max **3** fix attempts, then `node engine/engine.mjs block <T#> "<exact error + what you tried>"` and stop.
5. `node engine/engine.mjs done <T#> "<what was built + any decision, 2 sentences>"` — it re-runs every gate, marks the task, logs, and commits. A task is **not done** until this command succeeds.
6. Continue according to autonomy **phase** (`task` = stop now · `phase` = stop at phase end · `all` = continue until finished or blocked).

## 3. Quality gates (run by the engine, in order: typecheck → lint → test → build → audit)
- **typecheck**: `npm run typecheck`
- **lint**: `npm run lint`
- **test**: `npm test`
- **build**: `npm run build`
- **audit** (optional): `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`

Forbidden ways to "pass": suppressing type/lint errors, weakening or deleting tests, `skip`/`only`, catching and ignoring errors, mocking the unit under test. Report honestly when something can't be verified (e.g. third-party APIs without credentials).

## 4. Context & token discipline
- Never load whole documents "just in case". `5_CURRENT_TASK.md` carries the needed excerpts; open other sections only by heading.
- `node engine/engine.mjs status` is the cheap way to regain state after `/clear` (suggested after each **phase**).
- Gate output is already truncated to the failing tail; don't re-run commands just to see more unless needed.
- Prefer search (grep/glob) over reading large files; read the specific range you need.
- Keep chat replies short: what changed, gate result, next step.

## 5. Truthfulness & dependencies
- Never invent APIs, packages, flags or config keys. Check the **installed** version (lockfile / `node_modules` / site-packages) and its type definitions or official docs (use the context7 MCP if available).
- Before adding a dependency: confirm it exists, is maintained, and is compatible with the pinned toolchain (peer deps!). Pin it.
- If docs and reality disagree, trust reality, record it in `docs/8_DECISIONS.md`.

## 6. Security (every task, not just the audit)
- No secrets in code, tests, logs or commits. Read config from the validated env/config module only.
- New env var ⇒ add it with a DUMMY value to `.env.example` and to the architecture doc in the same task.
- Never edit `.env*` secret files (the engine blocks it); never `git add` them; never force-push or use `--no-verify`.
- Validate all external input at the boundary; parameterised queries only; least-privilege by default.

## 7. Scope changes & decisions
- Discovered work ⇒ `node engine/engine.mjs add-task "<Phase>" "<title | accept: … | files: … | refs: … | deps: …>"` — don't silently expand the current task.
- Architecture/library/trade-off decisions ⇒ one entry in `docs/8_DECISIONS.md` (context → decision → consequences).
- `node engine/engine.mjs approve …` records **human** approvals. Never run it yourself unless the human explicitly tells you to in this conversation.

## 8. Stack conventions
- TypeScript strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess; `any`, `@ts-ignore` and `eslint-disable` are forbidden (enforce `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error`).
- Validate every external input (HTTP, env, webhooks) with a schema library (e.g. zod) at the boundary.
- Read config only from a typed, validated env module; never `process.env.X` scattered in code.
- Pin exact dependency versions and check peer-dependency compatibility before adding a package.

## 9. Project rules
- Money is always integer minor units (cents/paise) end-to-end; format only at the edges.
- Stock changes go only through StockService (atomic conditional UPDATE + ledger); never write stock_levels directly.
- API tests run against real PostgreSQL; each test file gets a fresh schema via tests/helpers/db.ts — never reset the DB inside a test file.
- Every webhook verifies its signature on the raw body with a timing-safe compare and is idempotent on retries.
- Payment amounts are always computed server-side from the order; never trust an amount from the client or a callback URL.
- Shared domain types live in src/api/src/domain/types.ts and are imported by the web app (type-only).

## 10. Commands
- Install: `npm ci` · Dev: `npm run dev` · Deploy target: **azure-container-apps** (staging → production)
- Engine help: `node engine/engine.mjs help`
